subject: Physiotherapy in General Medical & Surgical Condition

questions.question: On ECG paper the smallest square (1 mm) represents:
questions.explanation: At 25 mm/s each small square is 0.04 s.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: On ECG paper the large square (5 mm) represents:
questions.explanation: Five small squares equal 0.20 s.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: On the vertical axis of ECG paper, each large square equals:
questions.explanation: One large square (5 mm) is 0.5 mV; one small square is 0.1 mV.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: On the vertical axis of ECG paper, each small square equals:
questions.explanation: 1 mm equals 0.1 mV at standard calibration.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Precordial lead V1 is placed at the:

options.A: 4th intercostal space at the right sternal border
options.C: 5th intercostal space at the mid-clavicular line
options.D: 4th intercostal space at the left sternal border

questions.explanation: V1 is right of the sternum in the 4th intercostal space.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Precordial lead V2 is placed at the:

options.A: 4th intercostal space at the left sternal border
options.B: 5th intercostal space at the mid-clavicular line
options.D: 4th intercostal space at the right sternal border

questions.explanation: V2 is left of the sternum in the 4th intercostal space.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Precordial lead V3 is placed:

options.B: 4th intercostal space at the right sternal border
options.C: 5th intercostal space at the mid-clavicular line

questions.explanation: V3 lies between V2 and V4.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Precordial lead V4 is placed at the:

options.B: Anterior axillary line at V4 level
options.C: 4th intercostal space at the left sternal border
options.D: 5th intercostal space in the mid-clavicular line on the left

questions.explanation: V4 is at the apex beat position.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Precordial lead V5 is placed at the:

options.A: 4th intercostal space at the left sternal border
options.B: 5th intercostal space in the mid-clavicular line
options.D: Anterior axillary line at the level of V4

questions.explanation: V5 lies on the same horizontal level as V4 in the anterior axillary line.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Precordial lead V6 is placed at the:

options.A: 4th intercostal space at the left sternal border
options.B: Mid-axillary line at the level of V4
options.C: Anterior axillary line at V4 level
options.D: 5th intercostal space in the mid-clavicular line

questions.explanation: V6 is in the mid-axillary line at the level of V4 and V5.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: On ECG, leads II, III and aVF correspond to the ______ wall of the heart.
questions.explanation: These leads look at the inferior wall (right coronary artery territory).
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: On ECG, leads V1 and V2 correspond to the ______ wall of the heart.
questions.explanation: V1-V2 view the interventricular septum.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: On ECG, leads V3 and V4 correspond to the ______ wall of the heart.
questions.explanation: V3-V4 view the anterior wall (LAD territory).
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: On ECG, leads I, aVL, V5 and V6 correspond to the ______ wall of the heart.
questions.explanation: Leads I, aVL, V5 and V6 look at the lateral wall (circumflex territory).
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: To calculate heart rate from a 6-second ECG strip, the number of QRS complexes is:
questions.explanation: A 6-second strip is one-tenth of a minute.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Normal sinus rhythm has a rate of:
questions.explanation: Below 60 is sinus bradycardia and above 100 is sinus tachycardia.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The normal range of the PR interval is:
questions.explanation: The PR interval is 3-5 small squares.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The normal range of the QRS complex is:
questions.explanation: A QRS wider than 0.12 s suggests bundle branch block or ventricular origin.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The P wave of the ECG represents:
questions.explanation: The P wave is atrial depolarisation.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The QRS complex of the ECG represents:
questions.explanation: QRS is ventricular depolarisation (atrial repolarisation is hidden within it).
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The ST segment of the ECG represents:
questions.explanation: The ST segment is the plateau after depolarisation and the start of repolarisation.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The T wave of the ECG represents:
questions.explanation: The T wave is ventricular repolarisation.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Following a zone of injury in the myocardium, the ECG change seen is:
questions.explanation: Acute injury (e.g. STEMI) causes ST-segment elevation.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Following a zone of infarction in the myocardium, the ECG change seen is:
questions.explanation: Infarcted myocardium is electrically dead, giving Q waves.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Pathological Q waves in leads V1 to V4 indicate:
questions.explanation: V1-V4 view the anterior wall.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Pathological Q waves in leads I and aVL indicate:
questions.explanation: Leads I and aVL view the high lateral wall.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Pathological Q waves in leads II, III and aVF indicate:
questions.explanation: Leads II, III and aVF view the inferior wall.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: With hypercalcaemia the QT interval is:
questions.explanation: Hypercalcaemia shortens the ST segment and QT interval.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: With hypocalcaemia the QT interval is:
questions.explanation: Hypocalcaemia prolongs the ST segment and QT interval.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which ECG change is seen in a person on digitalis?

options.C: All of these: ST depression, T wave flattening or inversion and QT shortening

questions.explanation: The digitalis effect gives scooped ST depression, T flattening and a short QT.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which ECG change is seen in a person on quinidine?

options.C: All of these: prolonged QRS, T wave flattening and long QT

questions.explanation: Quinidine widens QRS, flattens T waves and prolongs QT.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Mean arterial blood pressure is calculated as:
questions.explanation: MAP is about diastolic pressure plus one third of the pulse pressure.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: On the dyspnoea scale, a +1 grade is when dyspnoea is:

options.A: Severe so the patient cannot continue
options.B: Mild but noticeable to the observer
options.C: Moderate with the patient able to continue activity
options.D: Mild and not noticeable to the observer

questions.explanation: +1 mild, not noticeable; +2 mild, noticeable; +3 moderate; +4 severe.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: On the dyspnoea scale, a +2 grade is when dyspnoea is:

options.B: Moderate with the patient able to continue
options.D: Mild and noticeable to the observer

questions.explanation: +2 means mild difficulty that the observer can see.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: On the dyspnoea scale, a +3 grade is when dyspnoea causes:

options.C: Moderate difficulty but the patient can continue his activity

questions.explanation: +3 means moderate difficulty with activity still possible.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: On the dyspnoea scale, a +4 grade is when dyspnoea causes:

options.C: Severe difficulty so the patient cannot continue his activity

questions.explanation: +4 is severe breathlessness that stops the activity.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: On the angina scale, a +1 grade is when the pain is:

options.C: The most severe pain ever experienced

questions.explanation: +1 light, +2 moderate, +3 severe, +4 worst.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: On the angina scale, a +2 grade is when the pain is:

options.B: The most severe pain ever experienced

questions.explanation: +2 is moderate pain.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: On the angina scale, a +3 grade is when the pain is:

options.B: The most severe pain ever experienced

questions.explanation: +3 means the pain is severe and the patient would stop the activity.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: On the angina scale, a +4 grade is when the pain is:

options.D: The most severe pain ever experienced

questions.explanation: +4 is the worst angina the patient has ever had.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which type of angina is of a more intense form and occurs at less exertion force?
questions.explanation: Unstable angina is new or progressively worsening angina at lower exertion or at rest.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: When the pitting seen is less than 1/4 inch and the indentation is mild, the oedema is graded:
questions.explanation: 1+ mild pitting under 1/4 inch rebounds immediately.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In grade 2+ pitting oedema:

options.B: The pitting is 1/2-1 inch and lasts 15-30 seconds
options.C: The indentation is moderate with pitting of 1/4-1/2 inch that rebounds within 15 seconds
options.D: The pitting is over 1 inch and lasts over 30 seconds

questions.explanation: 2+ is moderate pitting that rebounds within about 15 seconds.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In grade 3+ pitting oedema:

options.B: The pitting is 1/4-1/2 inch and rebounds in 15 seconds
options.C: The indentation is severe with pitting of 1/2-1 inch that rebounds in about 15-30 seconds
options.D: The pitting is over 1 inch and lasts over 30 seconds

questions.explanation: 3+ is severe oedema with a deeper, slower-rebounding pit.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In grade 4+ pitting oedema:

options.D: The indentation is very severe with pitting of more than 1 inch lasting more than 30 seconds

questions.explanation: 4+ is very severe pitting oedema.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Compression therapy is contraindicated when the ankle-brachial index (ABI) is:
questions.explanation: Compression is unsafe in severe arterial disease (ABI below about 0.5).
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Compression therapy is to be used with caution when the ABI is:
questions.explanation: With moderate arterial disease only reduced compression is advised.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In a person with a platelet count below 20,000 cells/cubic mm, only ______ exercises are to be given.
questions.explanation: With very low platelets only activities of daily living are advised because of bleeding risk.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: An inferior wall myocardial infarction indicates occlusion of the ______ artery.
questions.explanation: The RCA supplies the inferior wall in most patients.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: A lateral wall myocardial infarction indicates occlusion of the ______ artery.
questions.explanation: The circumflex supplies the lateral wall.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: An anterior wall myocardial infarction indicates occlusion of the ______ artery.
questions.explanation: The LAD supplies the anterior wall and septum.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: For myocardial infarction, a window period of about ______ is effective to restrict the infarct size (thrombolysis).
questions.explanation: Reperfusion within about 6 hours salvages the most myocardium.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Systemic signs (ascites, peripheral oedema, weight gain, hepatomegaly) in addition to cardiac symptoms are seen in:
questions.explanation: Right-sided failure causes systemic venous congestion.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Signs of pulmonary congestion (dry cough, orthopnoea, wheezes) in addition to cardiac symptoms are seen in:
questions.explanation: Left-sided failure causes pulmonary venous congestion.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Cor pulmonale is ______ that occurs as a result of lung pathology.
questions.explanation: Chronic lung disease leads to pulmonary hypertension and right ventricular enlargement.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Goose neck deformity of the left ventricular outflow tract on angiography is a feature of:

options.B: Atrial septal defect (ostium primum / AV canal defect)

questions.explanation: The goose-neck sign is characteristic of endocardial cushion (primum ASD) defects.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which of the following is FALSE for chronic arterial insufficiency?

options.B: Pulses will be reduced or absent
options.C: There will be rubor on dependency
options.D: The affected extremity will be warm

questions.explanation: In arterial disease the limb is cool and pale on elevation with dependent rubor.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which of the following is FALSE for chronic venous insufficiency?

options.A: Elevation of the lower extremity will reduce pain
options.B: The skin will be dark and cyanotic
options.C: There will be rubor on dependency
options.D: The affected extremity will be of normal or elevated temperature

questions.explanation: Rubor on dependency is a sign of arterial, not venous, disease.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a contraindication for cardiac rehabilitation?

options.B: Resting systolic BP above 200 mm Hg
options.D: Resting diastolic BP above 110 mm Hg

questions.explanation: Stable post-MI patients are the main candidates; the other conditions are contraindications.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: For cardiac rehabilitation, which of the following is a contraindication?
questions.explanation: Unstable angina is a contraindication until stabilised.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Phase I of cardiac rehabilitation (inpatient) is typically for the initial ______ days.
questions.explanation: Phase I lasts only a few days in hospital.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In phase I of cardiac rehabilitation, exercises of ______ METs should be given.
questions.explanation: Phase I activity is low-level, about 1-3 METs.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which of the following leads to termination of an exercise programme?

options.C: A rise in systolic BP of 10 mm Hg

questions.explanation: Significant arrhythmias or conduction block, a drop in systolic pressure over 10 mm Hg or diastolic pressure over 110 mm Hg stop exercise.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In a cardiac transplant recipient (denervated heart), which measure should be used to monitor exercise intensity?
questions.explanation: The transplanted heart lacks vagal and sympathetic control, so the heart rate response is delayed and unreliable.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a positive effect of cardiac rehabilitation?

options.B: Increased myocardial contractility and oxygen supply

questions.explanation: Training increases stroke volume and lowers resting heart rate.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: When lymphoedema is reversible and the limb is pitting and soft, it is stage ______ of lymphoedema.
questions.explanation: Stage 1 (spontaneously reversible) shows pitting oedema that reduces on elevation.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: When lymphoedema is irreversible and the limb shows increased fibrotic tissue, it is stage ______ of lymphoedema.
questions.explanation: Stage 2 (spontaneously irreversible) has fibrosis and non-pitting swelling.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Extreme swelling with fibrosis and sclerosis (elephantiasis) is stage ______ of lymphoedema.
questions.explanation: Stage 3 (lymphostatic elephantiasis) has skin changes and gross enlargement.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which type of lymphoedema is one in which fluid leaks from cuts and wound healing is severely disturbed?
questions.explanation: Lymphorrhoea is leakage of lymph through the skin.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In manual lymphatic drainage, which congestion is cleared first?
questions.explanation: The proximal region is cleared first so that distal fluid has somewhere to drain.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The chest compression rate used in adult BLS is:
questions.explanation: Adult compressions are given at 100-120 per minute.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The depth of chest compression in adults during BLS is:
questions.explanation: Adult compressions should be at least 5 cm but not more than 6 cm deep.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The compression to ventilation ratio for adults during BLS is:
questions.explanation: One-rescuer and two-rescuer adult CPR both use 30 compressions to 2 breaths.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The normal (physiological) PEEP value applied in ventilated patients is about ______ cm H2O.
questions.explanation: Physiological PEEP of about 5 cm H2O replaces the loss of glottic closure.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: When PaO2 is 60-79 mm Hg, the hypoxaemia is:
questions.explanation: Mild hypoxaemia is 60-79 mm Hg.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: When PaO2 is 40-59 mm Hg, the hypoxaemia is:
questions.explanation: Moderate hypoxaemia is 40-59 mm Hg.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: When PaO2 is less than 40 mm Hg, the hypoxaemia is:
questions.explanation: Severe hypoxaemia is below 40 mm Hg.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which statement is TRUE for respiratory alkalosis?

options.A: pH decreases, PaCO2 is normal, HCO3 decreases and a cause is diarrhoea
options.B: pH increases, PaCO2 decreases, HCO3 is normal and the cause is alveolar hyperventilation
options.C: pH increases, PaCO2 is normal, HCO3 increases and a cause is vomiting
options.D: pH decreases, PaCO2 increases and the cause is alveolar hypoventilation

questions.explanation: Hyperventilation blows off CO2, raising the pH.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which statement is TRUE for respiratory acidosis?

options.A: pH decreases, PaCO2 is normal, HCO3 decreases and a cause is diarrhoea
options.B: pH increases, PaCO2 is normal, HCO3 increases and a cause is vomiting
options.C: pH increases, PaCO2 decreases and the cause is hyperventilation
options.D: pH decreases, PaCO2 increases, HCO3 is normal (acute) and the cause is alveolar hypoventilation

questions.explanation: CO2 retention from hypoventilation lowers the pH.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which statement is TRUE for metabolic alkalosis?

options.A: pH increases, PaCO2 decreases and the cause is hyperventilation
options.B: pH decreases, PaCO2 increases and the cause is hypoventilation
options.C: pH decreases, HCO3 decreases and a cause is diarrhoea
options.D: pH increases, PaCO2 is normal, HCO3 increases and one of the causes is vomiting

questions.explanation: Loss of gastric acid raises bicarbonate and the pH.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which statement is TRUE for metabolic acidosis?

options.A: pH decreases, PaCO2 is normal, HCO3 decreases and one of the causes is diarrhoea
options.B: pH increases, HCO3 increases and a cause is vomiting
options.C: pH increases, PaCO2 decreases and the cause is hyperventilation
options.D: pH decreases, PaCO2 increases and the cause is hypoventilation

questions.explanation: Bicarbonate loss or acid gain lowers the pH (uncompensated, PaCO2 normal).
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: According to GOLD, COPD with FEV1 below 80% but above 50% predicted is staged as:
questions.explanation: GOLD 1 FEV1 at least 80%, 2 is 50-79%, 3 is 30-49%, 4 below 30%.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: According to GOLD, COPD with FEV1 below 50% but above 30% predicted is staged as:
questions.explanation: GOLD stage 3 is severe airflow limitation.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: According to GOLD, COPD with FEV1 below 30% predicted is staged as:
questions.explanation: GOLD stage 4 is very severe airflow limitation.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Panacinar emphysema in a young non-smoker is associated with ______ levels of alpha-1 antitrypsin.
questions.explanation: Alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency allows unchecked elastase action and early emphysema.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT seen in pink puffers (emphysema)?
questions.explanation: Emphysematous patients are thin and cachectic with a barrel chest and minimal cough.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which test is the gold standard to confirm the diagnosis of cystic fibrosis?
questions.explanation: A sweat chloride above 60 mEq/L is diagnostic.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In which condition do the secretions of exocrine glands thicken, leading to obstruction?
questions.explanation: CFTR mutation produces thick secretions in the lungs, pancreas and sweat glands.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: A classic ground-glass pattern on chest X-ray is seen in:
questions.explanation: Surfactant deficiency causes a diffuse ground-glass appearance with air bronchograms.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In flail chest (multiple rib fractures), during inspiration the chest wall segment moves ______ and during expiration it moves ______.
questions.explanation: The flail segment shows paradoxical movement.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding pleural effusion is FALSE?

options.A: There is fluid in the pleural space
options.C: There is a problem in pleural reabsorption

questions.explanation: Effusion forms when hydrostatic pressure rises or oncotic (osmotic) pressure falls.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The postural drainage position for the apical segments of the upper lobes is:

options.D: Prone with pillows under the hips

questions.explanation: Apical segments drain with the patient sitting upright (no tilt).
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The postural drainage position for the posterior segments of the upper lobes is:

options.B: Sitting leaning forward over a pillow

questions.explanation: Leaning forward on a pillow drains the posterior upper lobe segments.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The postural drainage position for the anterior segments of the upper lobes is:
questions.explanation: Lying flat on the back drains the anterior upper lobe segments.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The postural drainage position for the lingula or right middle lobe is:

options.A: Supine, quarter-turned with the foot of the bed raised about 15 degrees

questions.explanation: The patient lies quarter-turned with the lung to be drained uppermost and head down.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The postural drainage position for the anterior basal segments of the lower lobes is:

options.A: Supine with the foot of the bed raised about 20 degrees

questions.explanation: The head-down tilt drains the basal segments.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The postural drainage position for the posterior basal segments of the lower lobes is:

options.C: Prone with the foot of the bed raised about 20 degrees

questions.explanation: Lying prone with the head down drains the posterior basal segments.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The postural drainage position for the lateral basal segment of the right lower lobe is:

options.A: Left side lying with the foot of the bed raised about 20 degrees

questions.explanation: The segment to be drained is uppermost with a head-down tilt.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The postural drainage position for the superior segments of the lower lobes is:
questions.explanation: The superior (apical) segments of the lower lobes drain with the patient lying prone and flat.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The correct sequence of autogenic drainage is:

options.A: Collect phase, evacuation phase, unstick phase
options.C: Evacuation phase, unstick phase, collect phase
options.D: Unstick phase, collect phase, evacuation phase

questions.explanation: Breathing at low lung volumes loosens mucus, mid volumes collect it and high volumes evacuate it.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The PEP used in low pressure positive expiratory pressure therapy is about:
questions.explanation: Low-pressure PEP uses 10-20 cm H2O; high-pressure PEP uses forced expiration against a mask.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The PEP used in high pressure positive expiratory pressure therapy (forced expiration against a mask) is up to:
questions.explanation: HP-PEP generates high pressures during forced expiration.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Pursed lip breathing is used primarily in:
questions.explanation: Pursed lips create back pressure that splints airways open and slows expiration.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: During coughing the glottis is ______ and during huffing it is ______.
questions.explanation: A cough begins with glottic closure; huffing keeps it open, so it is less tiring.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Inspiratory muscle training is usually started at about ______ of maximum inspiratory pressure (MIP).
questions.explanation: Initial IMT loads are about 30-40% of MIP and are progressed.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which device combines high-frequency oscillation with positive expiratory pressure to clear mucus from the airway?
questions.explanation: The Flutter device uses a steel ball in a pipe to oscillate airflow during expiration.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Compared with the Flutter device, the Acapella device is:

options.A: Not dependent on gravity (can be used in any position)

questions.explanation: Acapella uses a counterweighted lever so it works in any position.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The negative pressure applied during endotracheal suctioning in adults is about:
questions.explanation: Adults typically need 100-150 mm Hg; lower pressures are used in children.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Suction force should be applied for no longer than about:
questions.explanation: Prolonged suction causes hypoxia and atelectrauma.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The suction catheter size normally used in adults is:
questions.explanation: Adults use 10-16 French gauge catheters.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The suction catheter size normally used in newborns is:
questions.explanation: A 5-6 FG catheter suits neonates.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: With a tracheostomy tube in place, there is a ______ in dead space.
questions.explanation: Bypassing the upper airway reduces anatomical dead space.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The usual endotracheal tube size is ______ in women and ______ in men.
questions.explanation: Adult female tubes are 7.0-7.5 mm and male tubes 8.0-8.5 mm.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which mode is commonly used to wean a patient from mechanical ventilation?
questions.explanation: Synchronised intermittent mandatory ventilation lets the patient take over breaths progressively.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Oxygen therapy is of little use when hypoxaemia is due to:
questions.explanation: In a true shunt blood bypasses ventilated alveoli, so extra oxygen barely raises PaO2.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In an underwater seal chest drain, the tip of the drainage tube is kept about ______ below the water surface.
questions.explanation: A tip 2-3 cm under water acts as a one-way valve with minimal resistance.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The BODE index for COPD stands for:

options.A: Bronchodilator reversibility, Obesity, Dyspnoea, Exercise capacity

questions.explanation: BODE combines body mass index, airflow obstruction (FEV1), dyspnoea (MMRC) and exercise capacity (6MWD).
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In the BODE index, obstruction, dyspnoea and exercise capacity are measured respectively by:

options.A: FEV1 predicted, MMRC dyspnoea scale and 6-minute walk test
options.B: FVC, MMRC dyspnoea scale and 3-minute walk test
options.C: PEFR, Borg scale and stair climb
options.D: FEV1 predicted, MMRC dyspnoea scale and 12-minute walk test

questions.explanation: The BODE uses FEV1 percent predicted, the modified MRC scale and the 6-minute walk distance.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: A higher score on the BODE index means:

options.C: The condition is severe (higher mortality risk)

questions.explanation: Higher BODE scores predict increased mortality in COPD.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The study of factors which affect normal ageing and its effects is known as:
questions.explanation: Gerontology is the scientific study of ageing.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The branch of medicine that deals with illness of old age and its care is:
questions.explanation: Geriatrics is the clinical care of the elderly.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: With ageing, DNA synthesis and cell division:
questions.explanation: Cells reach a finite division limit (Hayflick limit), and replication slows with age.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which of the following statements is FALSE with respect to muscular changes seen in ageing?

options.D: Loss of type 1 fibres is the predominant change

questions.explanation: Ageing mainly causes loss and atrophy of fast-twitch type 2 fibres.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which of the following postural changes is NOT seen with ageing?
questions.explanation: The lumbar lordosis tends to flatten with age.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Senile macular degeneration is characterised by loss of:
questions.explanation: Macular degeneration damages the central retina, sparing peripheral vision.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In presbycusis, hearing loss is seen first at:
questions.explanation: Age-related hearing loss begins with high-frequency sounds.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which of the following statements is FALSE with respect to balance changes with ageing?
questions.explanation: Vestibulo-ocular reflex gain decreases with age.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: With ageing, all of the following increase in the cardiovascular system EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Coronary flow decreases with age while resistance and BP rise.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: With ageing, deposition of lipofuscin and degeneration of cardiac muscle give the heart a characteristic ______ colour.
questions.explanation: Brown atrophy of the heart is due to lipofuscin pigment.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: With ageing, all of the following ECG changes are seen EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Conduction slows with age; the QRS widens rather than narrows.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: With ageing, all of the following changes are seen in the pulmonary system EXCEPT:

options.A: Pulmonary blood vessels become less distensible
options.C: TLC remains the same or decreases slightly

questions.explanation: Residual volume increases with age as elastic recoil is lost.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Aerobic training in the elderly results in all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Training reduces resting heart rate and blood pressure.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which of the following changes is NOT seen in the integumentary system with ageing?
questions.explanation: Melatonin secretion falls with age.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which of the following changes is NOT seen in the renal system with ageing?
questions.explanation: Blood urea rises when GFR falls with age.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: To facilitate wound healing, energy intake should be maintained at about:
questions.explanation: Adequate calories prevent protein from being used for energy in wounds.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: To facilitate wound healing, protein intake should be maintained at about:
questions.explanation: Wound healing raises protein requirements to about 1.25-2 g/kg.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: When the platelet count is 20,000 per cubic mm or less, exercise is:
questions.explanation: Severe thrombocytopenia carries a high risk of spontaneous bleeding.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: BMI is calculated as:

options.A: Weight in kg divided by height in square metres
options.B: Height in metres divided by weight in kg
options.C: Weight in lb divided by height in square metres
options.D: Weight in kg divided by height in square centimetres

questions.explanation: BMI = weight (kg) / height (m) squared.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: A BMI of less than 18.5 is classified as:
questions.explanation: WHO: underweight below 18.5 kg/m2.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: A BMI of 18.5-24.9 is classified as:
questions.explanation: Normal BMI is 18.5-24.9.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: A BMI of 25-29.9 is classified as:
questions.explanation: BMI 25-29.9 is overweight (pre-obese).
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: A BMI of 30-34.9 is classified as:
questions.explanation: Class 1 obesity is a BMI of 30-34.9.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: A BMI of 35-39.9 is classified as:
questions.explanation: Class 2 obesity is a BMI of 35-39.9.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: A BMI of 40 or more is classified as:
questions.explanation: A BMI of 40 or above is class 3 (severe) obesity.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: For men, a waist circumference of more than ______ is associated with increased risk of cardiovascular conditions.
questions.explanation: A waist above 40 inches (102 cm) in men indicates central obesity.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: For women, a waist circumference of more than ______ is associated with increased risk of cardiovascular conditions.
questions.explanation: A waist above 35 inches (88 cm) in women indicates central obesity.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: While using a skinfold caliper, which is the most common site for skinfold measurement?
questions.explanation: Triceps, subscapular, suprailiac and thigh are standard sites.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: For an adult healthy male, the normal range of body fat is about:
questions.explanation: Healthy adult male body fat is roughly 12-20 percent.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: For an adult healthy female, the normal range of body fat is about:
questions.explanation: Healthy adult women carry more essential fat, about 18-28 percent.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams
